title: PostCSS
description: Transform CSS with PostCSS plugins: Autoprefixer, preset-env, cssnano, and Tailwind integration.

data.text: PostCSS is a CSS transformation pipeline. It parses CSS into an AST and runs plugins over it — which is how Autoprefixer adds vendor prefixes, cssnano minifies, and Tailwind generates utilities.

data.title: What happens on each build
items: Each CSS file is parsed once into a PostCSS AST.
Plugins run in order, each transforming the AST.
The serialiser writes the final CSS.
Bundlers (Vite, Webpack, Next.js) call PostCSS automatically when a config file exists.

data.caption: postcss.config.js — sensible defaults

data.title: Install the plugins and inspect the result
data.code:
npm install -D postcss postcss-cli autoprefixer postcss-preset-env cssnano postcss-import
npx postcss src/styles.css -o dist/styles.css --env production

data.text: Autoprefixer reads browserslist to decide which prefixes are still needed. In 2026 that list is short, but the same shared file also drives Babel and other tools, so keep it accurate rather than copying an old template.

data.caption: src/styles.css — modern CSS that PostCSS compiles

data.title: Plugin order matters
data.text: postcss-import must run before plugins that inspect imported files, and cssnano should run last. A mis-ordered pipeline produces output that looks fine until one specific syntax appears.

terms.definition: Abstract syntax tree — the tree PostCSS plugins traverse and mutate.
A PostCSS plugin that adds -webkit-/-moz- prefixes where browserslist requires them.
A CSS minifier and optimiser usually applied in production only.
A bundle of plugins that polyfills modern CSS syntax for your target browsers.

items.question: Is PostCSS a preprocessor like Sass?
items.answer: No. Sass has its own syntax and compiler; PostCSS transforms standard CSS (or Sass output) through plugins. Tools such as `postcss-scss` let PostCSS handle Sass syntax when needed.

items.question: Do I need a postcss.config.js?
items.answer: Only when you use plugins. Vite and Next.js process CSS out of the box; the config file is what enables prefixed, minified, and Tailwind-generated output.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: PostCSS is a plugin pipeline over a CSS AST.
Autoprefixer plus browserslist handle vendor prefixes.
cssnano should be production-only and last in the order.
Tailwind v4 is itself a PostCSS plugin now (@tailwindcss/postcss).
data.takeaway: Framing PostCSS as a pipeline (not a framework) is the accurate and interview-friendly description.
